fspParties.note: The Dominican Republic's FSP member is the Partido de la Liberación Dominicana (PLD), founded by Juan Bosch and listed on Regalado's 2008 roster. In government the PLD governed as a broadly centrist, pro-business party — its FSP affiliation is documented, though analysts note its policy record is not straightforwardly left. It held the presidency 1996–2000 and 2004–2020 and lost power in 2020.

legislativeControl.seats: The PLD was a rising third force behind Balaguer's PRSC and the PRD; it first won the presidency in 1996.
The PLD held the presidency for all but one term (2000–2004) and commanded large congressional majorities in both chambers through the 2000s–2010s, peaking at roughly two-thirds after 2016.
legislativeControl.notes: Except for the 2000–2004 PRD interlude, when the PLD sat in opposition.

legislativeControl.seats: The PLD lost the 2020 presidency and its congressional majority to Luis Abinader's PRM (which won its own majorities again in 2024); the PLD is now a diminished opposition party.

parties.name: Fuerza del Pueblo, PRSC, PRD and minor parties

government.note: The end of 16 years of PLD rule: the FSP member fell from 106 to 75 seats and lost the presidency. The PLD had also split — Leonel Fernández's breakaway Fuerza del Pueblo drew away part of its vote. The PRM alone (86 of 190) fell just short of an absolute majority, but with allied minor parties the incoming Abinader government controlled the chamber (per CSIS) and swept most Senate races.
The PLD won an outright majority (106/190) in its own right and, with allied parties in its 'Bloque Progresista', controlled well over two-thirds of the chamber.
The PLD held 26 of 32 Senate seats — a commanding supermajority.
